definition: Generous and forgiving, especially toward a rival or weaker person.
example: He made a magnanimous offer to forgive the debt.
nuance: Magnanimous emphasizes nobility of spirit, not physical size.
prompt: A winner responds to a rival's criticism.
options: Magnanimous in victory, she praised her rival and dismissed the insult.
Magnanimous in victory, she humiliated her rival repeatedly.
Her magnanimous gesture was an act of petty revenge.
She was magnanimous because she won by a large margin.
reasons: Grace and generosity toward a rival show magnanimity.
The size of a victory does not establish character.

practice.prompt: A younger brother accidentally breaks his older sister's prized model ship.
options: The family's vote to repair the ship was magnanimous, with every single hand raised at the dinner table.
She was magnanimous about the ship, refusing to speak to her brother for the rest of the month.
Too magnanimous to confess, her brother hid the splintered pieces of the ship under his bed.
She was magnanimous about the broken ship and helped her tearful brother glue the mast back on.
reasons: This confuses the word with unanimous; a vote everyone agrees on is not generosity.
Holding a monthlong grudge is the opposite of a forgiving, generous response.
Hiding a mistake out of fear has nothing to do with generosity toward someone else.
Forgiving a younger sibling and helping repair the damage shows a big-hearted spirit.
